Adepta Sororitas.description: Built around Morvenn Vahl leading a dense mass of cheap, fast melee bodies — Arco-Flagellants, Celestian Sacresants, Sanctifiers, and Ministorum Priests stacking Act of Faith triggers — with the Triumph of Saint Katherine and Celestian Insidiants providing mid-board pressure and miracle dice manipulation. This is a Champions of Faith-adjacent body-flood engine that wins by cramming high-OC melee units onto every objective by turn 2 while miracle dice smooth out critical wound rolls and Act of Faith activations generate extra movement and attacks. It punishes static gunlines and transport-heavy lists that struggle to clear waves of T3 bodies with FNP stacking and 4+ invuln on Sacresants before the melee connects. It cracks open against mobile anti-armour and Lethal Hits-heavy shooting that burns through the fragile wound pools before the Arco-Flagellant charge delivers.

Adeptus Custodes.description: Built around Shield-Captain on Dawneagle Jetbike leading Vertus Praetors as the primary damage engine, with Allarus Custodians and a Telemon Heavy Dreadnought providing mid-board weight, this is a Solar Spearhead-adjacent jetbike hammer that delivers elite bodies onto objectives at 14" move while the Telemon anchors the backfield. The list wins by bullying primary scoring through raw OC dominance and 4+/5++ durability — Vertus Praetors contest mid-table turn 1, Allarus deepstrike onto pressure points, and the Navigator's psychic denial shuts down opponent utility windows. It punishes static gunlines and transport-infantry lists that can't match the Praetors' threat range, as concentrated AP-3 Lance fire and Hurricane Bolter volume strip transports before their cargo can deploy meaningfully. Dedicated Melta and anti-armour overload from mobile vehicle lists cracks it open, since the 4+ invuln on jetbike chassis doesn't hold against repeated S8+ AP-3 focus fire and the low model count bleeds activations fast.

Adeptus Custodes.description: Built around Witchseekers, Prosecutors, and Vigilators delivered inside Venerable Land Raiders and Anathema Psykana Rhinos, this is the allied Sisters of Silence transport-mech expression of Lions of the Emperor — a Custodian Guard hammer backed by a Null-Maiden delivery chassis. The plan is to disgorge anti-psyker melee elites from transports into midfield on turn two while Custodian Guard hold primary objectives, generating consistent scoring through activation volume that pure Custodes lists can't match. The transport shell punishes opposing melee-commitment armies — once a Land Raider drops Witchseekers and Vigilators onto an exposed unit, the Deny-the-Witch bubble and high-attack-count blades clean up anything short of a true anvil, and the Rhino chassis absorbs overwatch that would otherwise strip the Sisters before they engage. Concentrated anti-tank fire cracks this list open before the transports reach engagement range, since the Venerable Land Raiders and Rhinos are the entire delivery mechanism and losing them early leaves the Sisters walking across an open board.

Adeptus Custodes.name: Dreadnought Hammer

Adeptus Custodes.description: Built around a core of Contemptor-Achillus and Contemptor-Galatus Dreadnoughts supported by Telemon heavies and a Custodian Guard screen, this is the Solar Spearhead expression Custodes players run when they want T7-8 chassis with 4+ invulns doing the heavy lifting rather than infantry bricks. The engine is delivering multiple Dreadnoughts into mid-board simultaneously — the Achillus closes for melee while the Galatus walls an objective and the Telemon's Arachnus Blaze Cannon chips vehicles at range — generating Primary through sheer OC density that no single unit can answer. It punishes Mid-T brawlers and Transport Infantry lists that commit expensive hammers into 4+/5++ Dreadnought bodies that simply don't die to one round of focused fire, forcing unfavorable multi-turn trades. Against Mobile Anti-Armour opponents with concentrated AP-3+ Melta, however, T7-8 chassis without a repair mechanism folds faster than the win rate suggests it can absorb.

Astra Militarum.description: Built around Scout Sentinels, Hellhounds, a Rogal Dorn Commander, and Leman Russ Exterminators supported by a Tech-Priest Enginseer, this is a Mechanised Assault variant that fuses Grizzled Company-style heavy firepower with fast scout harassment — a forward-pressure gunline rather than a static castle. The plan is to use Scout Sentinels to strip cover and screen-bust early while Hellhounds and the Exterminator's autocannon volleys clear infantry, freeing the Rogal Dorn to concentrate AP-3+ fire on elite or vehicle targets. It punishes mid-T brawlers and transport-infantry lists hard — Hellhound flamers and Exterminator autocannons shred T5 mobs and Rhino-mounted infantry before they can close, while the Dorn's bulk absorbs counter-fire. It cracks under sustained anti-armour focus: concentrated Melta or Knight-speed mobility can isolate and strip the Dorn and Exterminators before the Enginseer's repair economy compensates, collapsing the damage engine.

Black Templars.description: Built around Marshal-led Sword Brethren squads supported by Castellan and Emperor's Champion buffs, delivered alongside Repulsor Executioners and Assault Intercessors in the Righteous Crusaders detachment, this is a hybrid fire-and-faith list that marries mid-range heavy firepower with aggressive melee delivery. It scores by using the Repulsor Executioner's Macro-plasma incinerator and heavy laser destroyer at 36–48" to strip elite chassis and vehicles, then crashing Sword Brethren — stacked with Marshal re-rolls and Emperor's Champion Crusader's Wrath — into whatever survives. It punishes static gunlines and transport-infantry mirrors that can't simultaneously absorb AP-3+ ranged volume and a Sword Brethren counter-punch with Devastating Wounds access. It cracks open when fast skimmer lists or mobile anti-armour vehicles dictate engagement range, denying the list its preferred mid-range fire band and picking apart the relatively low model count before the melee wave can connect.

Blood Angels.description: Built around Death Company Marines with Jump Packs, Death Company Dreadnought, and Sanguinary Guard led by Lemartes and Astorath, this is a Liberator Assault Group hammer — fast jump-pack elites crashing into mid-board on turn 1 with Chaplain litany stacking and Death Company's Black Rage trigger. The engine is threat saturation: Lemartes' Rites of Battle buff plus Astorath's aura push Death Company to hit on 2s with Lethal Hits procs, letting multiple independent melee hammers land simultaneously so the opponent can't prioritize their defensive resources fast enough to hold primary. It punishes static or slow-footprint opponents — Heavy Gunline and Transport Infantry lists that can't reposition once multiple AP-2/AP-3 jump-pack units are already in their face across every objective. The win rate, though, signals what cracks it: without durable screens or a ranged threat, it collapses against anything that can shoot it off the board before the charge lands — Mobile Anti-Armour or Skimmer Fire lists that stay at 18"+ range and pick apart the unprotected 3+/no-invuln Death Company before Lemartes' bonus means anything.

Chaos Daemons.description: Built around Bloodletters in massed blobs, Bloodcrushers as the elite hammer, and a character stack of Bloodmaster, Rendmaster on Blood Throne, and Skullmaster cycling Khornate buff auras, this is Blood Legion doing exactly what the detachment name promises — a Khorne melee tide that layers mobility tricks on top of raw volume. It scores primary by flooding mid-board objectives with high-OC Bloodletter blobs that hit back in melee, then uses Bloodcrushers and Flesh Hounds as fast flanking hammers to isolate and delete opposing scoring units before they can answer. The 9.2 Layered Lethal Combat loading is the mechanical teeth: Lethal Hits triggers on Bloodletter Hellblades combined with the character aura stack means high-T targets that expect to absorb a melee charge and survive often don't, punishing durable mid-range brawlers (T5-6 Ork mobs, Plague Marines) that can't absorb mortal-wound-equivalent spill. At roughly 49% win rate, the cracks show against fast anti-armour and kiting lists — Flesh Hounds and Bloodcrushers are fast but not fast enough to catch a 14" Raider, and with no shooting whatsoever the list bleeds primary every turn a skimmer denies the engagement.

Chaos Daemons.description: Built around Lords of Change, Kairos Fateweaver, and Be'lakor screening a dense swarm of Screamers and Flamers, this is the Shadow Legion at its most overwhelming — a Tzeentch-heavy Daemonic Incursion variant that floods the board with fast, invuln-stacked bodies backed by elite psychic heavy-hitters. The engine is tempo and attrition: Screamers' 16" movement and 5+ invuln contest mid-board objectives from turn one while Flamers and Lords of Change spike concentrated Lethal Hits volume into whatever the opponent commits to clearing them, with Be'lakor's -1 to-hit aura shielding the entire formation from efficient return fire. It punishes static gunlines and transport-infantry lists hardest — Heavy Gunline Toolbox can't reposition out of the Screamer flood, and Pactbound Zealots' crit-shooting bounces off the 5+ invuln stack when the hits are being suppressed by -1. Fast mobile anti-armour like Mont'ka Crisis suits or Chaos Knights crack it open, matching the swarm's movement while delivering the AP-3+ Melta volume needed to burn through T5 Daemon bodies before Be'lakor's aura can compensate.

Chaos Daemons.description: Built around Rotigus, a Great Unclean One, and dense Plaguebearer blobs backed by Beasts of Nurgle and Poxbringer character support, this is a Plague Legion list that weaponizes Nurgle's layered defensive toolkit — Disgustingly Resilient, Grandfather's Blessing, and the Contagion aura — to grind opponents into the dirt across five turns. The win condition is smothering midfield objectives under T4 Plaguebearer masses with sticky-objective behavior, letting Rotigus and the Great Unclean One generate mortal wounds and Lethal Hits pressure while the horde absorbs return fire through stacked FNP equivalents and sheer wound volume. It punishes Heavy Gunline and Transport Infantry matchups hardest, where blast templates can't clear Plaguebearer blobs fast enough before the scoring gap becomes irreversible and T9 Greater Daemons absorb the anti-armour budget that should be cracking transports. Fast mobile lists — Mont'ka Battlesuits, Chaos Knights with AP-3 melta, and anything that matches the army's movement while hitting T9 chassis through Melta or concentrated AP-3-plus fire — crack it open by dictating engagement range before Rotigus closes and denying the Contagion aura that makes the whole defensive stack function.

Chaos Space Marines.description: Built around Vashtorr the Arkifane leading a Soulforged Warpack of Venomcrawlers, Defilers, and Forgefiends, with a Warpsmith keeping the engines running and Cultist mobs screening the advance — this is a daemon-engine-heavy CSM list that fuses mobile anti-armour punch with a self-sufficient mechanicus support stack. The engine is Vashtorr's Dark Pact amplification on daemon vehicles: Forgefiends with +1 to wound on ranged contracts delete T7-9 chassis at mid-range, Venomcrawlers close distance to lock melee, and Defilers threaten both arcs while Cultists flood objectives to sustain primary scoring. It punishes low-model-count vehicle lists and planted gunlines hard — the Forgefiend's AP-2 autocannon volume plus Defiler battle cannon Blast templates overwhelm Russ companies and Knight-support builds that can't screen every angle simultaneously. It cracks when flooded by fast melee or massed Melta at close range, where the daemon engines' modest invulns (5+ on most chassis) and lack of a durable infantry hammer leave the screen stripped and the expensive vehicles exposed before Vashtorr's buffs can cycle.

Chaos Space Marines.description: Built around Huron Blackheart, Abaddon the Despoiler, Chosen squads, and Defilers in the Red Corsairs Raiders detachment, this is Huron's Marauders at its most maximalist — a sprawling, multi-threat list that blends transport-delivered elite infantry with daemon-engine fire support and one of the game's most punishing character stacks. The engine is Huron's Masters of the Maelstrom stratagem economy feeding Abaddon's combat output and Chosen's Devastating Wounds crit-chain, while Defilers hold midfield and generate enough threat vectors that the opponent can't prioritize correctly across a single turn. It punishes static gunlines and low-activation armies hardest, where the sheer number of distinct threat types forces poor target-priority decisions and the Defiler's indirect-adjacent firing arcs keep no position truly safe. Concentrated anti-elite firepower — specifically AP-3+ with high damage per shot aimed at Abaddon or Huron early — collapses the character engine that holds the whole damage spike together.

Dark Angels.description: Built around Azrael leading Inner Circle Companions and Deathwing Knights, supported by Land Speeder Vengeances and Scout Squads as the forward screen, this is the Inner Circle Task Force delivering a hybrid hammer-and-fire platform — elite Terminator melee packed behind a mobile shooty shell. The engine scores by shuttling Deathwing Knights into mid-board contact via Azrael's aura buffs while Land Speeder Vengeances suppress opposing screens with Assault-keyword plasma, freeing the Companions to punch holes in anything that tries to contest. It punishes mid-range infantry and transport-heavy lists hard — the Speeder Vengeance's plasma fire picks apart Rhino-rush attempts before the cargo deploys, and Inner Circle Companions with AP-3 melee clean up whatever survives. At 48% win rate it's clearly skating a knife's edge, and the weakness is obvious: fast anti-armour pressure from Knights or Mont'ka Crisis Battlesuits can strip the Speeders before the Deathwing brick closes range, collapsing the scoring engine entirely.

Dark Angels.description: Built around Land Speeder Vengeances, Ravenwing Black Knights, and Ravenwing Command Squads supported by Outriders and Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes, Company of Hunters is a fast mech-cavalry force that delivers anti-armour firepower on the move rather than from a firing line. The engine is speed-leveraged target deletion: Plasma Talon and Corvus Hammer pressure from Black Knights closes melee, while Land Speeder Vengeance Plasma Storm Batteries and Thunderstrike heavy weapons strip T7-9 chassis at range, scoring primary through superior board presence and activation volume across multiple fast units. Slow or static gunlines are punished hardest — the Ravenwing chassis matches or exceeds skimmer mobility while carrying AP-2 and AP-3 weapon profiles that strip Russ-equivalent armor before they can dictate range. The list cracks open when faced with concentrated anti-vehicle fire that can crack T5-6 bike and speeder chassis at distance, or melee tarpits with enough bulk to lock multiple Outrider or Black Knight units simultaneously and grind down the activation count advantage.

Drukhari.description: Built around Wyches, Reavers, and Incubi delivered in Raiders and Venoms with a Succubus at the helm, this is a Wych Cult-flavored Realspace Raiders shell that marries the fire-and-fade chassis of Skimmer Skirmish Fire with genuine close-combat teeth. The plan is to ferry high-attack-volume melee units into engagement range on turn 2 via Raider disembark, spike opposing elites with Incubi's AP-2 cleave and Wych Cult Combat Drug bonuses, then fade back into Venom cover while Reavers harvest secondary objectives on the flanks. It punishes planted-gunline and slow durable-grind lists hard — anything that can't kite back watches its fire bases get locked in melee while Reavers Bladevane-sweep Behind Enemy Lines scoring unopposed. Fast anti-armour lists are the problem: a Knight or Mont'ka player matching its 14"-move chassis with AP-3+ Melta pops Raiders before the cargo deploys, collapsing the entire delivery engine in turn 1.

Emperor's Children.description: Built around Infractors, Flawless Blades, and Noise Marines delivered in transports with a Lord Exultant and winged Daemon Prince of Slaanesh providing the command stack, this is the Emperor's Children Carnival of Excess in its most complete form — a Rhino-rush melee hammer dressed in Slaaneshi excess, hitting every profile on the table. The plan is to crack open mid-board turn 2 with Infractors and Flawless Blades disembarking into AP-2 melee swings stacked with the Lord Exultant's crit-amplifying aura, while Noise Marines lay down S5 Assault-keyword fire to screen-strip whatever the transports can't reach, and the Daemon Prince hunts characters with Precision. It punishes heavy gunlines and low-model-count anti-armour lists brutally — the transport delivery bypasses firing arcs, and the mixed melee-plus-shoot profile means there is no clean defensive answer for a Russ company or a 5-Knight list that can't engage in two phases simultaneously. The fragility shows against massed anti-transport shooting and against volume-horde lists that can absorb the melee spike, strip the transport screen, and out-OC the Emperor's Children across five objectives while Infractors are still walking forward on foot.

unitFrequency.datasheet: daemon prince of slaanesh with wings

Emperor's Children.description: Built around massed Daemonettes delivered alongside Fiends, a Keeper of Secrets, and a Lord Exultant, this is a Carnival of Excess-style Emperor's Children melee hammer that floods the mid-table with high-volume S4 Daemonic attacks amplified by Slaanesh's signature charge-and-pile-in tricks. The engine is pure activation saturation: multiple large Daemonette units plus Fiends claim objectives by turn 2, the Defiler and Lord Exultant provide anti-armour threat that forces difficult targeting decisions, and Infractors clean up whatever survives the initial wave. It punishes static gunlines and transport-infantry lists that can't generate enough defensive activations to hold every contested marker simultaneously — the sheer OC volume from Daemonette blobs outscores opponents who spread to answer the threat. Against Layered Lethal Combat lists running stacked FNP and 2+/4++ saves, the S4 AP-0 core of the Daemonette damage profile bounces off efficiently, and a single bad charge roll on the Keeper collapses the turn's damage ceiling entirely.

enhancementFrequency.name: Deeds that Speak to the Masses

Genestealer Cult.description: Biosanctic Broodsurge built around Purestrain Genestealers as the melee hammer, Neophyte Hybrid blobs as the scoring backbone, and Reductus Saboteurs plus Achilles Ridgerunners providing ranged disruption across a wide, mixed-profile roster. The plan is to flood objectives with Neophyte OC while Purestrains deepstrike or infiltrate into the opponent's scoring units turn 1-2, using Acolyte Hybrids with hand flamers as a secondary melee wave that punishes anything that survives the first contact. It punishes slow, positional lists — Heavy Gunline and durable-grind archetypes struggle to clear the combination of 4+ invuln Purestrains and layered Neophyte bodies before the scoring deficit becomes unrecoverable. Fast anti-armour lists and mobile kiting factions crack it open, as the low invuln coverage on Neophytes and the fragile Ridgerunner chassis evaporate under concentrated AP-3+ fire before the melee wave can close.

Grey Knights.description: Built around Paladin Squads, Brotherhood Terminators, and a Grand Master character stack led by Voldus, this is a Hallowed Conclave expression that leans into the Mobile Toolbox pattern — teleporting elite infantry into mid-board while Interceptors provide flanking threat and secondary coverage. The win condition is concentrating Paladin and Terminator melee into isolated targets after a turn-1 deepstrike or teleport commit, with Voldus and the Brotherhood Chaplain stacking damage and Fight on Death buffs to make each trade cost the opponent more than it costs you. The 2+/4++ chassis across every model punishes skimmer-fire lists that can't volume through those saves, and the Interceptor mobility locks secondaries that slow armies can never contest. The list struggles against Layered Lethal Combat and Transport Infantry — Pactbound crit-stacking with Precision drops the character stack that powers the damage engine, and a Cultist screen absorbs the deepstrike before the Possessed counter-punch walks through the exposed Terminators.

Grey Knights.description: Built around Grand Master Nemesis Dreadknight and Nemesis Dreadknight chassis supported by Castellan Crowe's Purifier synergy, this is Sanctic Spearhead running a hybrid mobile-control shell — big Dreadknight threats up front, Purifiers and Strike/Interceptor squads spreading across objectives behind them. The engine scores by using the GMNDK's Teleport Strike delivery and Interceptor repositioning to contest mid-board objectives while Purifiers' Warp Shaping and Crowe's Heroic Sacrifice ability create a resilient scoring layer that grinds primary across five turns. The list cracks open against concentrated Melta or AP-3+ mobile firepower — Knights or Mont'ka Crisis Battlesuits can strip the Dreadknight chassis before the infantry scoring engine has time to establish, leaving Strike Squads holding objectives against threats they can't reliably clear.

Imperial Knights.description: Built around a Knight Castellan anchor flanked by Armiger Warglaives and Knight Destrers, this is a Skyreaper Lance-style mixed-chassis Imperial Knights list running the Castellan's Volcano Lance and Plasma Decimator as a long-range T9+ deletion platform while Warglaives close distance and Helverins provide mid-range anti-armour cover. The engine is concentrated AP-3+ and Melta-equivalent fire focused sequentially on the opponent's most dangerous unit each turn — Castellan cracks the T9-12 chassis, Warglaives and Destrers mop up whatever survives and contest midfield objectives while the big knights free-fire from the rear. It punishes Layered Lethal Combat lists hardest — Death Guard Vectorium and Custodes Talons can't absorb sustained Volcano Lance hits through FNP or 4++ when S16 AP-4 Damage 8 simply bypasses the invuln math, and the Armiger skirmish line prevents the opponent from trading into the Castellan's flanks. Against Mid-T Mixed Brawler hordes and Transport Infantry lists the activation gap bites hard — 30-Boyz mobs or Pactbound Zealots Cultist screens absorb the Knight punch on sheer model count, lock Warglaives in melee tar-pits, and grind primary scoring while the five-activation Knight list can't contest three objectives simultaneously.

Imperial Knights.description: Built around massed Armiger Warglaives and Helverins supported by a Knight Castellan and Cerastus Knight Lancer, this is the Skyreaper Lance expression of Imperial Knights — a swarm of fast T9 chassis with 4+ ion-shield invulns replacing the traditional single-Titanic anchor with activation volume. The game plan is to exploit 10"+ Armiger movement and the Castellan's long-range Volcano Lance to strip opposing anti-armour targets early, then convert activation superiority into primary-scoring dominance as the opponent's damage-dealers disappear. Concentrated AP-3+ Melta and Reaper Chainsword melee from Warglaives punishes low-model-count elite lists and Mobile Anti-Armour mirrors that can't match the activation count, while the Helverin autocannon batteries chip infantry screens efficiently enough to stay clean on objectives. The critical weakness is mid-board mob tarpits — War Horde Boyz blobs and Beast Snagga Squighogs close the distance and lock Armigers in melee where their shooting output drops to zero, and the list's 8–10 activation ceiling still loses the primary-scoring race against Transport Infantry lists flooding objectives with 30–40 bodies.

Imperial Knights.description: Built around Armiger Warglaives and Helverins as a massed light-cavalry screen, backed by a Cerastus Knight Lancer, Knight Castellan, and Knight Crusader as the heavy strike core, this is the Freeblade Company running the full Imperial Knights roster depth — fast cheap chassis flooding mid-board while titanic guns do the killing. The engine is speed-differential exploitation: Warglaives use their 10" move to lock opposing priority targets in melee while the Castellan's Volcano Lance and Crusader's Avenger Gatling Cannon delete whatever the Lancer's AP-3 charge doesn't finish, all backed by Helverin autocannon fire peeling screens at range. Ion shields (4+ invuln) stacked across every chassis means concentrated anti-armour fire has to commit an unreasonable volume to clear even one Knight, punishing small-activation elite lists like Custodes or Death Guard that can't generate enough AP-3+ Melta shots to out-trade the field. The weakness is mob tarpits and activation-count armies — War Horde Squighogs or Pactbound Zealots Cultist screens can lock Warglaives in melee turns 1–2, bleeding the Crusader's firing window while volume bodies outscore the five-activation Knight list on objectives.

unitFrequency.datasheet: ironkin steeljacks with heavy volkanite disintegrators

Leagues of Votann.description: Built around Hearthkyn Warriors packed into Sagitaur transports, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn heavy-weapon teams, and an Arkanyst Evaluator-fueled damage engine, this is the Hearthband's armoured midfield brawler — a compact T5 force that plays somewhere between War Horde and Grizzled Company, delivering mixed-profile squads under fire and supporting them with planted heavy firepower. The gameplan is to advance Sagitaurs onto mid-board objectives turn 1, disgorge Hearthkyn and Ironkin Steeljacks into melee while Thunderkyn and Brôkhyr Iron-Masters deliver sustained AP-2 supporting fire, grinding primary scoring through sheer OC density and layered trade efficiency. It punishes transport-heavy mid-range lists where its volume of T5 bodies, FNP-equivalent Ancestor Grudge durability, and Sagitaur threat saturation overwhelms activation-starved opponents who can't clear multiple scoring units per turn. It struggles badly against Heavy Gunline Toolbox expressions — Russ Demolisher cannons and Blast templates systematically strip Hearthkyn blobs before the Sagitaurs can close, and the list has no speed advantage to escape planted firing arcs.

Leagues of Votann.description: Built around Einhyr Hearthguard bricks led by a Kâhl and Einhyr Champion, screened by Hernkyn Pioneers and backed by Brôkhyr Thunderkyn and Ironkin Steeljacks with Heavy Volkanite Disintegrators, this is the Hearthband's Hearthguard Hammer — a T5 elite-melee army with a credible mid-range shooting backstop. The engine is straightforward: advance Hearthguard onto midfield objectives behind Pioneer screening, trigger Judgment Tokens to stack wound-roll buffs, and let the Kâhl's Ancestral Grudge chain amplify melee output while Thunderkyn and Steeljacks punish anything that tries to counter-charge or hold at range. It punishes mid-T mixed brawler and volume-horde lists that think bodies alone win primary — Hearthguard at T5 with 4+ invuln absorb the mob counter-punch while Volkanite Disintegrators erase infantry screens faster than War Horde can replace them. Fast mobile lists and kiting skimmer armies expose the weakness: Pioneers lack the speed to protect flanks against 14"+ chassis, and once Hearthguard are isolated without Judgment Token support, their damage output per point drops sharply against armies that won't stand still and be hit.

Leagues of Votann.description: Built around Cthonian Beserks and Berehk Stornbröw delivering a Judgement Token-stacked melee hammer, with Einhyr Hearthguard and a Hekaton Land Fortress providing the armoured backstop, this is a Hearthband list that plays like a War Horde with a gunline safety net. The engine is Berehk's personal Judgement Token generation feeding Beserks into melee with Lethal Hits and Sustained Hits 1 already active, while the Hekaton and Sagitaurs hold fire lanes and drain opposing anti-tank resources that should be targeting the infantry hammer instead. It punishes mid-range brawler lists and anything that wants to grind attrition — the Judgement Token burst makes T5-6 infantry disappear in a single charge activation, and the Land Fortress absorbs the anti-armour attention that would otherwise strip the melee core. It struggles against fast skimmer lists and mobile anti-armour, where a 14"-move Raider or Knight chassis can dictate range, avoid the Beserk charge window, and pick apart the relatively low-movement Votann delivery.

Necrons.description: Built around two or three Doomsday Arks anchored by the Silent King, with Lokhust Heavy Destroyers and a Hexmark providing anti-armour and character-deletion support, this is the Starshatter Arsenal castle — a static long-range fire platform wrapped in Necron durability tricks. The engine scores by planting the Silent King on a mid-board objective to claim and sticky it while Doomsday Ark volleys (S14 AP-5 D6+6 at full health) delete priority targets at range, with Tomb Blades screening the flanks and Flayed Ones threatening deepstrike punishment against anything that pushes forward to clear the line. It punishes other planted gunlines and Transport Infantry hardest — the Silent King's Command Protocols stack onto Doomsday Arks firing into Rhino columns, and AP-5 ignores every Marine-equivalent save while the Hexmark's auto-hit profiles strip characters precision-style before the shooting phase resolves. The core weakness is anything fast enough to collapse the firing distance: Mobile Anti-Armour lists like Infernal Lance Knights can close 12" per turn and begin melting T8 hulls before the Arks can reposition, and the list has limited bodies to delay that engagement once the Flayed One screen is consumed.

Necrons.description: Built around Lokhust Destroyers, Skorpekh Destroyers, Ophydian Destroyers, and their paired Lords anchored by Nekrosor Ammentar, this is the Cursed Legion running its full Destroyer Cult stack — every unit in the list feeds the chain-buff engine that grants all Necrons +2 Strength when a Destroyer Cult unit destroys or halves an enemy unit. The plan is to sequence Lokhust gauss fire into a priority target turn 1, trigger the +2 Strength cascade, then crash Skorpekhs and Ophydians into whatever was already weakened — scoring primary through mid-board presence backed by Reanimation-sustained bodies that refuse to die on attrition. The 4+ invuln-equivalent durability across the Destroyer chassis and high base movement punishes static heavy gunlines that can't pivot fast enough to clear reanimating T5-6 elites before the Strength buff proc cascades through the entire army. The list cracks when it faces volume-fire Transport Infantry or Layered Lethal Combat walls — Pactbound Zealots crit-shooting strips Destroyer models faster than Reanimation can recover them, and FNP-stacked Death Guard Plague Marines absorb the +2 Strength spike without flinching.

Necrons.description: Built around Illuminor Szeras and a deep Canoptek support suite — Wraiths, Scarab Swarms, Canoptek Reanimators, and Technomancers stacking reanimation buffs — this is Awakened Dynasty playing the toolbox game at its most character-dependent. The engine is Szeras turbocharging Wraiths and Scarabs into near-unkillable mid-board anchors via stacked reanimation and the Void Dragon as a roaming anti-vehicle hammer, while the Scarab swarm volume floods objectives and forces the opponent to choose what to clear. Wraiths with a 4+ invuln and Reanimator-assisted resurrection punish any army that leans on volume AP-1/AP-2 fire to clear mid-board presence, and the Scarab blob creates an OC floor that expensive shooting lists can't efficiently address. The critical vulnerability is the character chain itself — lose Szeras or the Technomancer keeping Wraiths alive and the durability engine collapses, leaving T5 models without their FNP-equivalent buffer against AP-3+ Melta or concentrated Lascannon fire that hard-removes rather than chips.

Necrons.description: Built around two or more C'tan Shards — typically the Nightbringer and Transcendent C'tan as the primary killers, with the Deceiver and Void Dragon rounding out the roster — this is the Awakened Dynasty C'tan castle that floods the board with T10+ demigods hiding behind Flayed Ones screens and a Hexmark Destroyer for deep-strike denial. The engine is raw threat saturation: each C'tan demands a different answer (the Nightbringer's mortal-wound spray, the Void Dragon's anti-armour melee, the Transcendent's ranged bombardment), and when the opponent can't address all of them simultaneously, one walks onto an objective and holds it with 4+ invuln and double-digit wounds. The layered defenses — 4+ invuln across the C'tan roster, T10 chassis laughing off AP-1 and AP-2 chip, and Flayed Ones screen denying melee access — punish mid-T brawlers and anything relying on volume attacks to grind through the board. Concentrated AP-3+ Melta from a Knight-density list is what cracks it open, since the C'tan's invuln doesn't fully compensate for repeated high-damage Melta hits forcing failed saves across a small model count.

Necrons.description: Built around Skorpekh Destroyers, Skorpekh Lord, Ophydian Destroyers, and Lokhust Heavy Destroyers under Nekrosor Ammentar's leadership, Cursed Legion runs the full Destroyer Cult stack — every Destroyer Cult model gains +2 Strength, and each time one of your units destroys or halves an enemy, every other Necron infantry and cavalry unit on the board picks up +2 Strength for the rest of the turn. The plan is to use Ophydians' deepstrike and Skorpekhs' high base movement to isolate and chain-kill targets in sequence, triggering the cascade buff repeatedly while Lychguard and the Skorpekh Lord anchor mid-board objectives under reanimation. It punishes static gunlines and low-model-count vehicle lists that can't prevent melee engagement — once an Ophydian squad drops into a flank and cracks one unit, the +2 Strength ripple makes every subsequent combat that turn dramatically more lethal. However, layered defensive lists like Pactbound Zealots with Cultist screens absorb the deepstrike, and FNP-stacked or 2+/4++ armies soak the burst-damage window before the chain-buff can compound enough kills to matter.

Necrons.description: Built around a Skorpekh Lord driving a Skorpekh Destroyer hammer supported by Lokhust Heavy Destroyers, a C'tan Shard of the Void Dragon, and Technomancer-buffed durability, this is the Awakened Dynasty's wide-roster toolbox expression — fast melee threat paired with Reanimation-stacked resilience and meaningful anti-armour range. The engine scores by maneuvering the Skorpekh brick into mid-board objectives turn 1-2 behind the C'tan's threat bubble, using Lokhust Heavy Destroyers to strip T9+ vehicles at range while the melee core contests primary and dares the opponent to commit. It punishes static gunlines and fragile skimmer lists that can't trade into 4+ invuln plus Reanimation across multiple activations, and the Void Dragon's anti-vehicle output means pure armour spam can't simply hide behind T10+ chassis. The Achilles heel is layered-defense attrition lists — Death Guard Vectorium's Disgustingly Resilient plus Plagueburst Crawler indirect fire grinds the Skorpekh brick down before it clears Plague Marines, and any opponent who screens the forward deployment zone denies the turn-1 engagement the list needs to establish tempo.

Necrons.description: Built around the Lokhust Lord leading doubled-up Lokhust Destroyer squads, Lokhust Heavy Destroyers, Ophydian Destroyers, and Nekrosor Ammentar's +2 Strength chain-buff trigger, this is Cursed Legion at its most focused — a pure Destroyer Cult engine where every unit qualifies for the kill-chain bonus. The plan is to use Ophydians' deepstrike or Lokhust mobility to isolate and remove a key target each turn, triggering Cursed Legion's army-wide +2 Strength buff and converting the snowball into primary-scoring dominance as the opponent's hammers evaporate. Against Heavy Gunline Toolbox lists the Destroyers close faster than Russes can reposition, their Heavy Destroyer Gauss Destructor profiles hitting T9 chassis on 3+ to wound with AP-3, and the kill-chain trigger amplifies every subsequent activation. It cracks open against Transport Infantry or Layered Lethal Combat opponents — a screen of Cultists absorbs the Ophydian deepstrike, and Death Guard Plague Marines with Disgustingly Resilient shrug off AP-3 chip damage long enough to deny the Cursed Legion trigger and grind primary unchallenged.

Necrons.description: Built around a Lokhust Lord leading Lokhust Destroyers amplified by Nekrosor Ammentar, with Ophydian Destroyers and a Skorpekh Lord providing melee threat and a Canoptek Reanimator keeping the whole engine alive, this is Cursed Legion at its most focused — a Destroyer Cult spike list that leverages the +2 Strength chain-buff to punch well above its weight class against mid-tier armor. The kill chain is Nekrosor's buff triggering the Cursed Legion cascade, turning Lokhust gauss fire into a reliable anti-vehicle answer while Ophydians threaten flanks and lock down secondary objectives through sheer teleport positioning. At 79% win rate across its games, it punishes static heavy gunlines and skimmer lists hardest — the reanimation support from the Canoptek Reanimator keeps Lokhust squads contesting under return fire, and the 4+ invuln on Skorpekh elites makes clearing the board deeply inefficient for AP-1/AP-2 profiles. It folds to layered lethal combat lists: Disgustingly Resilient Death Guard and 2+/4++ Custodes absorb the gauss volume without triggering favorable trades, and the list's character dependency means losing Nekrosor Ammentar early collapses the Strength-buff cascade entirely.

Orks.description: Built around wall-to-wall Boyz mobs supported by Painboy-buffered durability, Big Boss and Warboss character stacks, and Stormboyz as the fast flanking threat, this is War Horde running its purest Green Tide expression — overwhelming body count delivered on foot, not in transports. The engine is total OC dominance: Sustained Hits 1 on every melee weapon means even basic Slugga Boyz generate real damage output while the sheer wound pool forces the opponent to spend every activation clearing mobs rather than contesting objectives, letting the list outscore on primary through attrition. It punishes low-activation vehicle lists and planted gunlines hardest — the 60-plus-body wave simply has more activations than a Russ company or a Knight lance can address, and Painboy Feel No Pain keeps key mobs alive through a turn of focused fire that would clear a normal unit. Fast skimmer lists are the natural crack — Drukhari Raiders and Aspect Host Dark Reapers can chip Boyz at range with Lethal Hits ignoring the Painboy save, kiting outside charge range until the mob's damage window closes entirely.

unitFrequency.datasheet: big mek with shokk attack gun

Orks.description: Built around Big Meks with Shokk Attack Guns, Tankbustas, Flash Gitz, and Lootas delivered in Trukks with Breaka Boyz screening, this is a War Horde variant that bends the faction's Sustained Hits 1 blanket toward a surprisingly credible shooting game. The plan is to park the Big Mek's randomized-but-high-volume Shokk Attack Gun in a protected backfield position while Trukks rush Tankbustas into melta range of priority vehicles and Lootas plus Flash Gitz provide a sustained fire base that chips everything else, generating enough primary scoring through sheer body count to stay ahead on the clock. Where it shines is against T7-9 vehicle-heavy lists — concentrated Tankbusta Rokkit Launchers hitting on 2s against VEHICLE targets combined with Melta range delivery punishes low-model-count anti-armour builds that can't absorb that much dedicated anti-tank volume across multiple delivery vectors simultaneously. The hard counter is anything with Blast templates and range, particularly AM Grizzled Company Demolishers and Punishers that clear the Breaka Boyz screen on turn one, strand the Trukks before they unload, and outright delete the static Lootas and Flash Gitz before they fire a meaningful second turn.

Orks.description: Built around Beastboss-led Beast Snagga Boyz and Squighog Boyz delivered by Trukks, screened by Gretchin and topped up with standard Boyz, Da Big Hunt drives this list — a dense Beast Snagga roster that weaponizes Trukk-rush delivery alongside the detachment's anti-vehicle specialization. The engine is closing distance fast: Trukks push Beast Snagga Boyz into midfield objectives by turn 2 while Squighog Boyz threaten early charges on heavy chassis, generating primary scoring through sheer OC volume that Beastboss aura buffs keep alive longer than expected. It punishes low-activation vehicle lists and slow durable gunlines — the activation gap and multi-threat charge vectors make it nearly impossible for a 4-6 chassis army to trade efficiently against 12+ units of T5-6 bodies with native anti-vehicle bite. Fast kiting armies are the hard counter: Drukhari Reaper's Wager and Aeldari Aspect Host can sit at 24"+ and chip mobs with Lethal Hits or Dark Lance fire without ever entering the Beast Snagga charge window.

Orks.description: Built around Wazdakka Gutsmek leading a pack of Warbikers and Deffkoptas, with Deffkilla Wartrikes and Wartrakks filling out the fast-attack core, this is Kult of Speed in everything but name — a high-velocity Ork swarm that hits midfield by turn 1 and never lets the opponent dictate range. The engine is raw board saturation: T5 bikes with Sustained Hits 1 from War Horde's always-on detachment ability flood every objective simultaneously, forcing the opponent to split fire across a dozen fast-moving threats while Stormboyz drop in to seal contested markers. It punishes static gunlines and Transport Infantry lists hardest — the sheer activation count and advance-and-shoot mobility means Russ companies and Rhino-rush CSM can't clear enough bodies before the primary scoring gap becomes insurmountable. Against Skimmer Skirmish Fire and Layered Lethal Combat the wheels come off: Drukhari can kite the 14" bike move indefinitely, and Death Guard Plague Marines backed by Plagueburst Crawler indirect simply shrug off AP-1 bike attacks through Disgustingly Resilient while grinding the primary race back.

Orks.description: Built around Mozrog Skragbad riding into battle alongside Squighog Boyz, Beast Snagga Boyz, a Kill Rig, and a Beastboss on Squigosaur, this is Da Big Hunt at full expression — a Beast Snagga-exclusive melee hammer that brings T6-7 bodies across every slot. The engine is closing distance with high-toughness cavalry and monsters, triggering Beast Snagga anti-vehicle bonuses on whatever the Kill Rig and Squighogs can pin, while Gretchin hold home objectives so every Beast Snagga unit commits forward to score primary through combat presence rather than passive hold. Squighog Boyz' combination of T5, 4+ save, and volume attacks with Devastating Wounds punishes low-activation vehicle lists and mid-T elite infantry that can't clear the threat in a single activation. The critical vulnerability is high-AP blast firepower — Dark Reaper Lethal Hits stacks and Russ Demolisher cannons chew through T6 Squighog models faster than Disgustingly Resilient would, and without transports or deepstrike, the approach lanes are exposed to a full round of concentrated fire before the charge lands.

Orks.description: Built around Beast Snagga Boyz and Squighog Boyz led by a Beastboss, with Gretchin and regular Boyz filling out a massive infantry footprint, this is Da Big Hunt pushed to its logical extreme — a wall of T5 bodies with raw OC that buries the board under sheer model count. The engine is mob volume: Beast Snagga Boyz claim and hold objectives through weight of wounds while Squighog Boyz threaten early charges against vehicles and monsters, closing the gap before the opponent can dictate the engagement. Planted shooting lists and anything relying on activation-count parity suffer most — 12-plus squads hitting the midfield simultaneously forces inefficient trades and gives up primary scoring to the mob every turn the opponent spends trying to clear bodies. The hard counter is blast-heavy firepower: Demolisher Cannons, Pulveriser Cannons, and Russ Battle Cannon templates clear eight to fifteen models per activation, and the lack of meaningful invulnerable saves means AP-2 shooting cuts through T5 efficiently enough to collapse the scoring base before the Squighogs can reach melee range.

Space Marines (Astartes).description: Built around Vulkan He'stan and Adrax Agatone stacking Melta and Flamer buffs across Infernus Squads, Eradicators, and a Land Raider Redeemer, this is a Firestorm Assault Force expression that weaponises the Promethean Cult keyword across every activation. The engine is concentrated thermal-weapon delivery: Vulkan's re-roll-wounds-of-1 on Melta and Flame weapons turns Eradicator Melta Rifles and Redeemer Flamestorm Cannons into reliable elite-killers, while the Redeemer deposits Infernus Squads into point-blank Flamer range on turn two to strip mid-board screens and force sticky-objective contests. It punishes durable medium-toughness infantry and transport-heavy lists brutally — AP-2 Melta and auto-hitting Flamers ignore the cover and invuln stacking that MSU Marine or Rhino-rush lists rely on to survive. Against fast kiting platforms (Drukhari Raiders, Wave Serpents) and high-volume horde screens the list struggles, because the Redeemer's 12" Flamestorm arc can be denied by repositioning and the Infernus payload never connects if the opponent refuses engagement outside 9".

Space Marines (Astartes).description: Built around Terminator Assault Squads and Terminator Squads led by a Librarian in Terminator Armour and an Ancient, this is a 1st Company Task Force — dense, short-range firepower delivered by walking bricks with 2+/5++ saves and teleport deep-strike threat. The win condition is reserving Terminators off-board to dictate engagement, dropping into mid-table turn 2 with the Librarian's psychic buffs active, then using Sternguard as a flexible backfield anchor to hold primary while the Terminator hammers score on contact. It punishes static gunlines and transport-mech lists that can't reposition fast enough to escape a mid-board teleport drop, since AP-3+ Storm Bolter volume plus Thunder Hammer mortals overwhelm anything relying on a 3+ save. Conversely, fast kiting lists — Drukhari Raiders and Aeldari Wave Serpents — can deny the engagement entirely by staying outside the Terminators' 5" threat bubble, and any list matching its melee output with layered invulns or FNP will grind the low-model-count brick off objectives over time.

Space Marines (Astartes).description: Built around Repulsor Executioners and Ballistus Dreadnoughts anchored by Marneus Calgar and his Victrix Honour Guard bodyguard, this is the Blade of Ultramar's signature hybrid: a planted heavy-firepower core wrapped in enough mobile infantry to contest every zone. Scout Squads and Intercessors handle the objective crust while the vehicles unload AP-2 to AP-3 volume from deployment or second-row positions. The engine is simple — Calgar's aura buffs keep the Repulsors and Ballistus Dreadnoughts hitting on rerolls while Scout screens deny deepstrike and Intercessors bank primary, forcing the opponent to either contest the infantry and eat the guns or hunt the guns and concede the board. The multi-chassis firepower spread punishes low-model-count armies — Knights, Mont'ka Battlesuits, and durable elite lists that can't absorb sustained AP-3 heavy bolter and macro-plasma incinerator fire across multiple activations. Massed melee hordes and aggressive melee toolboxes that can lock the Repulsors in combat remove the shooting entirely, and any list that can crack the Honour Guard bubble early undermines Calgar's reroll economy faster than the vehicles can compensate.

unitFrequency.datasheet: marneus calgar in armour of antilochus

Space Marines (Astartes).description: Built around Land Speeders, Storm Speeder Hammerstrikes, and Vindicators backed by Eradicators, this is an Ironstorm Spearhead-style mobile gunline that trades model count for concentrated anti-armour firepower across fast chassis. The engine is target-priority saturation: Hammerstrikes deliver Melta and missile fire from 12"+ movement platforms while Vindicator Demolisher Cannons (S14 AP-3 D6+1) crack anything that tries to castle, and Eradicators with heavy bolters clean up exposed infantry — all scoring primary through Incursor screens holding midfield objectives. It punishes planted static armies and slow vehicle gunlines badly, matching or exceeding their range while denying the firing-arc control that Russ companies and siege builds depend on, and the anti-armour density overloads single-layer defensive saves on T7-9 chassis. The main crack is activation count — against Transport Infantry or Mass Volume Horde lists that flood objectives with 12-15 squads, the Land Speeder Gunline simply can't contest enough markers simultaneously, and losing even one Hammerstrike early collapses the anti-armour budget before primary scoring stabilizes.

Space Marines (Astartes).name: Victrix and Friends

unitFrequency.datasheet: marneus calgar in armour of antilochus

Space Marines (Astartes).description: Built around Marneus Calgar leading Victrix Honour Guard as a near-unkillable melee anchor, flanked by Bladeguard Veterans and Lieutenant-buffed Intercessors delivering bodies to objectives, with Scout Squads handling forward screening and secondary scoring. The engine is Calgar's ability to keep Victrix stubbornly planted on mid-board objectives while Bladeguard threaten counter-punches and the scoring infantry saturate primaries — the list wins by making the central zone prohibitively expensive to contest while quietly banking secondaries on the flanks. Its mixed-axis profile (heavy weapons backstopping a durable melee core) punishes slow grind lists that can't simultaneously clear the Victrix brick and answer the Scout infiltration pressure on secondaries. Lists with genuine mobility — fast anti-armour vehicles or kiting skimmers — can sidestep the Calgar anchor entirely, dictating engagement range and bleeding the list out on primary before it can close.

units.rawBlock: • 10 Wulfen with Stormfrag auto-launcher and Thunder hammer

Space Wolves.description: Built around Thunderwolf Cavalry and Wulfen with Storm Shields as the melee hammers, with Wolf Guard Terminators providing elite depth, Scout Squads screening forward, and a Gladiator Lancer anchoring anti-tank — this is Champions of Russ doing the Wolf Jail thing without fully committing to it, spread across too many axes to own any single identity cleanly. The plan is to use Thunderwolves' 10" move to threaten midfield charges by turn 1 while the Lancer handles T9+ priority targets at range and the Wulfen absorb the counter-punch behind 4+ invuln Storm Shields. It punishes lists that rely on a single defensive layer — heavy gunlines can't stop both the melee wave and the Lancer's AP-4 on the same activation sequence, and static infantry blobs get tarpitted by a Thunderwolf unit that won't cleanly die. The diffuse playstyle signature is also the crack: elite melee-mech counters (Transport Infantry walls of Cultists screening Possessed, or mobile anti-armour with concentrated Melta focus-firing the Thunderwolves before they connect) expose how thin the list spreads across seven different playstyle axes with no dominant engine.

Space Wolves.description: Built around Wolf Guard Terminators, Wolf Guard Headtakers, and Bjorn the Fell-Handed anchoring a mixed-arms infantry core of Blood Claws and Grey Hunters delivered via transport, Saga of the Beastslayer plays as a mid-range assault force that refuses to commit to a single archetype — part Rhino-rush mech, part durable melee hammer, part mobile fire platform. It wins by flooding objectives with high-OC battleline bodies while Terminators and Headtakers disembark to threaten elite kills, with Bjorn providing a durable long-range anchor that forces the opponent to either shoot the Dreadnought or let the infantry swarm score freely. The multi-axis profile punishes opponents who build narrow counters — a player prepared for skimmer kiting or static gunlines finds themselves overwhelmed by mid-board body count and melee spike damage from T5 armored elites dropping Lethal Hits attacks. The same generalism is the weakness: without a dominant single engine, a focused alpha strike from concentrated AP-3+ anti-armour fire or a mass-volume horde that simply out-bodies the pack on objectives can expose the list's inability to win the attrition race it didn't choose to fight.

T'au Empire.description: Built around a Coldstar Commander leading Crisis Starscythe and Fireknife Battlesuits with Pathfinder and Stealth Battlesuit forward screens, this is Mont'ka at its sharpest — Jump-Shoot-Jump fire combined with Riptide anchor pressure into a coordinated multi-vector threat package. The engine is Coldstar-driven positional aggression: Pathfinders mark priority targets with Markerlight stacks, the Coldstar closes to Melta range and repositions before return fire arrives, and Crisis Battlesuits pile on AP-3+ anti-armour volume while Stealth Suits deny deepstrike corridors and hold flanking objectives. It punishes static gunlines and fragile skimmer lists brutally — planted Russ companies and Raider-borne Drukhari both lack the speed to deny JSJ repositioning or absorb concentrated Melta spikes turn after turn. However, mob-volume lists like War Horde or Pactbound Zealots with Cultist screens expose the low model count: with 12-15 opposing activations to your 8, the primary scoring race tips away fast once your Crisis Suits are forced to commit rather than kite.

T'au Empire.description: Built around the Twin Lance's paired heavy railguns anchoring a firebase of Broadside Battlesuits and Riptides, screened by Pathfinder Teams, Stealth Battlesuits, and fast Piranhas — this is Mont'ka's mobile-anti-armour expression, running jump-shoot-jump Crisis-style repositioning on heavier chassis than the typical Retaliation Cadre shell. The engine is target-priority deletion: Pathfinders mark a priority target with Markerlight stacks, the Twin Lance and Broadsides concentrate AP-3+ railgun and HYMP fire onto T7-9 vehicles and elite infantry in sequence, while Riptides and Piranhas contest midfield objectives and deny deep-strike corridors turn over turn. It punishes static gunlines and low-mobility armor lists severely — any list that can't reposition away from the railgun firing arcs gets dismantled piece by piece before it can score meaningful primary. The weakness is volume: against mass-infantry hordes or mobile toolbox lists that flood objectives with T5-6 bodies or melee threats that outrun the Piranha screen, the low activation count and fragile Pathfinder markers mean the damage engine stalls while primary bleeds away.

T'au Empire.description: Built around Riptides, Broadsides, Commander in Coldstar, and Crisis Starscythe Battlesuits screened by Stealth Suits and Pathfinders, this is the Mont'ka expression of T'au — mobile anti-armour firepower on fast chassis that Jump-Shoot-Jump out of reprisal range every turn. The engine is volume anti-tank: Broadsides and Riptides anchor kill zones while the Coldstar Commander and Crisis Suits use JSJ to spike priority targets with AP-3+ and Melta-equivalent profiles before repositioning behind LoS, with Pathfinder Markerlight stacks amplifying hit rates on the most critical activations. It punishes Heavy Gunline Toolbox and slow durable lists badly — planted Russ companies can't match the movement budget, and concentrated rail and fusion fire deletes T9 chassis before they generate return value. It struggles against Mass Volume Horde pressure and anything that floods objectives faster than the low-model-count T'au roster can contest, where the activation gap forces hard choices between shooting windows and primary scoring.

T'au Empire.description: Built around Commander in Coldstar Battlesuit, Crisis Sunforge Battlesuits, and a Riptide anchoring the backfield, the Experimental Prototype Cadre pairs elite T'au battlesuit technology with a surprisingly muscular Kroot ground game — Kroot Carnivores screening and Krootox Rampagers delivering mid-board T5 melee bulk. The engine is speed-dictated anti-armour pressure: Coldstar JSJ repositioning drops Sunforge Melta within 12" of priority targets each turn while the Kroot mass holds objectives and forces the opponent to split their threat assessment between fast-moving battlesuits and an advancing brawler screen. It punishes static gunlines and heavy-vehicle lists particularly hard, as the Coldstar's 20" move denies safe firing arcs while Sunforge AP-4 Melta reliably cracks T9-10 chassis that can't disengage. The list's critical vulnerability is high-activation melee aggression — Pactbound Zealots or War Horde mobs that can absorb a Melta volley and still deliver a turn-2 charge swamp the Kroot screen before the battlesuits can reposition, collapsing the primary scoring base the Carnivores are supposed to hold.

Thousand Sons.description:
Built around Rubric Marines, Sekhetar Robots, and Scarab Occult Terminators stacked under multiple Sorcerer characters, this is the Hexwarp Thrallband doing what its post-Grotmas detachment was designed for: layering Tzeentchian invulnerable saves (5+ native, pushed toward 4+ via Sorcerer auras) onto durable T4-5 bodies with Lethal Hits access through the faction's psychic-weapon profiles.

The engine scores by planting Rubrics and Scarab Occult on mid-board objectives while Sekhetar Robots and Tzaangor Enlightened with Fatecaster Greatbows generate Lethal Hits pressure at range, chipping opposing anchor units until Sorcerers in Terminator Armour drop Infernal Fusillade-equivalent damage spikes into isolated targets.

The invuln stack punishes Mid-T Brawlers and Mass Volume Hordes hardest — T5 Ork mobs and Cadian blobs can't generate enough AP to bypass layered 4+ invulns plus Disc-Sorcerer re-roll auras before Rubrics lock primary.

Fast mobile lists that skip engagement entirely crack this open: a Reaper's Wager kite or Mont'ka JSJ battlesuit column stays outside the Lethal Hits envelope and bleeds Rubrics off objectives turn by turn, exploiting the army's near-zero base movement.

Thousand Sons.description: Built around large Rubric Marine blobs, Scarab Occult Terminators, Magnus the Red, and Sekhetar Robots cycling through Cult of Magic's Cabal of Sorcerers strat chain, this is a Cult of Magic list that uses depth of roster — Tzaangor Enlightened ranged harassers, Infernal Master aura support — to look like a toolbox while actually functioning as a body-count scoring engine. The win condition is planting T4 3+/5++ Rubric blobs on objectives with Sorcerous Pact buffs active, using Magnus and the Terminators as a mid-board hammer that demands immediate anti-elite answers, then grinding primary while the opponent's resources are divided. It punishes mobile anti-armour and skimmer lists that struggle to clear FNP-stacked, 5++ invuln infantry efficiently — Rubrics and Scarab Occult both absorb AP-2 chip fire and require either dedicated volume or AP-3+ to shift per turn. It cracks against concentrated heavy gunline pressure — Demolisher Cannon Blast templates and Russ Eradicator fire ignore the invuln spread and strip Rubric squads faster than the Cabal Sorcerers can cycle Smite damage back into primary scoring tempo.

exalted sorcerer on disc of tzeentch

Thousand Sons.description:
Built around Sekhetar Robots, Defilers, and Forgefiends supported by Exalted Sorcerers on Disc and a Daemon Prince of Tzeentch with Wings, this is a mobile daemon-engine heavy list that plays closer to a Chaos Knights roster than a traditional Thousand Sons psychic shell — every anchor unit is a T9+ chassis or a flying character moving 12"+ per turn.

The engine is AP-3+ firepower from multiple angles simultaneously: Forgefiend autocannon volleys and Defiler battle cannons plant suppressing fire downfield while the Sekhetar Robots close range to melta targets, with the Daemon Prince and Disc Sorcerers threatening flanks and character-sniping via Precision crits stacked on Tzeentch-mark attacks.

It punishes Heavy Gunline Toolbox and Transport Infantry lists hard — the combination of indirect Defiler fire, mobile Forgefiend threat presence, and fast-flanking characters denies both static firing positions and Rhino-rush delivery lanes before the opponent can establish their trade rhythm.

It cracks open against Mid-T Mixed Brawler and Mass Volume Horde lists, where Ork mob tarpits or AM infantry blobs lock the daemon engines in melee or flood objectives faster than a low-activation-count vehicle roster can contest them, bleeding primary across turns 3 and 4 while the list's shooting goes to waste clearing bodies rather than scoring.

Tyranids.description: Built around Broodlord-led Genestealer blobs with Lictor, Deathleaper, and Von Ryan's Leapers flooding in from every reserve angle, the Assimilation Swarm is Tyranids' premier infiltration-pressure list. The engine is Subterranean Assault-style positioning: get a threat into an unexpected table quarter every turn, force the opponent to react to multiple simultaneous infiltrate and deep-strike vectors rather than contest objectives cleanly, and grind primary while they're constantly firefighting. The 4+ invuln-equivalent durability on Genestealers and the sheer model-count pressure punishes heavy gunline lists that can't clear multiple 20-body blobs per turn before primary bleeds. Where it cracks open is into Lethal Hits stacks and layered durable defenses — Plague Marine walls with Disgustingly Resilient shrug off the charge math that Genestealers rely on, and anything that can reliably spike mortal wounds through volume ignores the infiltrate threat entirely.

Tyranids.description: Built around Psychophages, Pyrovores, the Norn Assimilator, and a Haruspex supported by Ripper Swarm screening, this is an Assimilation Swarm list leaning hard into the faction's most underplayed bio-horror melee chassis. The engine is closing mid-board through a Ripper screen while the Norn Assimilator and Haruspex apply T10+ pressure that forces the opponent to split anti-tank fire between two distinct high-wound threats, with Psychophages and Pyrovores cleaning up infantry screens via their Torrent and Lethal Hits-adjacent flame profiles. It punishes Heavy Gunline and Transport Infantry lists that lack sufficient anti-horde volume, because clearing Ripper Swarms while simultaneously threatening the big monsters demands more shooting activations than those lists typically budget. Fast mobile lists and anything stacking AP-3+ Melta can strip the Norn Assimilator before it connects, and the list's near-zero invulnerable save coverage across most units means a focused alpha strike finds no defensive layers to bounce off.

Tyranids.description: Built around Tyranid Primes with Lash Whips leading Hormagaunt blobs, with Raveners, Hyperadapted Raveners, and a Trygon punching up through the Vanguard Onslaught subterranean delivery system, this is an underground-assault melee swarm that floods the board from unexpected angles. The engine is turn-1 and turn-2 deepstrike saturation — Trygon burrowing creates an arrival point for Raveners and The Red Terror to emerge mid-table, while Hormagaunt masses claim home objectives and dare the opponent to commit firepower to clearing bodies rather than contesting primary. It punishes static gunlines and heavy-vehicle lists hardest, since the multi-wave underground delivery denies firing arcs before they can be established and the sheer wound pool of 50-70+ T3-4 models forces inefficient trades against Blast-light rosters. The list cracks open against Lethal Hits stacks and volume-shooting archetypes — Grizzled Company Demolishers and Punishers clear Hormagaunt blobs faster than they can be replaced, and Death Guard Contagion debuffs strip the toughness margin that makes the swarm's melee trades work.

Tyranids.description: Built around Exocrines and Tyrannofexes firing behind a living tide of Termagants, Hormagaunts, and Gargoyles, this is the Invasion Fleet's Synaptic Imperative engine expressed through ranged bio-artillery — a monster-gunline shell wrapped in a mass-screening swarm. The plan is to plant the big-bug shooters at range, use the Tervigon to endless-spawn Termagants onto mid-board objectives for total OC dominance, and let the Exocrine's bio-plasmic cannon and Tyrannofex's acid spray grind whatever survives the screen. It thrives against slow durable lists and mobile anti-armour builds that can't efficiently clear a 40-60 body blob fast enough to contest primary before the shooting eats their key chassis. It struggles against Heavy Gunline Toolbox opponents — Russ Demolisher blast templates and Punisher cannons are purpose-built to delete exactly these screen-and-anchor formations before the bio-artillery can reposition or the Tervigon replenishes losses.

Tyranids.description: Built around Screamer-Killers, Norn Emissary, Maleceptor, and a dense screen of infiltrating harassment units — Neurolictors, Von Ryan's Leapers, and Deathleaper — this is an Invasion Fleet-style mobile monster mash that weaponizes early board presence rather than turn-1 shooting weight. The engine is forward-deploying infiltrators to deny opponent deployment and screening zones, then funneling Screamer-Killers and the Norn Emissary into isolated targets through the gaps, with Maleceptor's psychic denial locking out key stratagems at the moment of engagement. It punishes static gunlines and low-activation vehicle lists that can't contest multiple infiltration threats simultaneously — the 9" pre-game moves force reactive deployment, and T9 Screamer-Killers with 4+ invuln absorb the return fire that planted Russ or Devastator stations try to deliver. Where it cracks is into Plague Marine or Custodian bricks with layered FNP and 2+/4++ saves: the monster-strike damage ceiling isn't high enough per activation to clear 2+/4++ models efficiently, and the list bleeds primary while grinding through durable midfield anchors.

World Eaters.description:
Built around Bloodletters, Flesh Hounds, Bloodcrushers, Skarbrand, and a Lord on Juggernaut backed by a Defiler, this is a Goretrack Onslaught-style daemon-cavalry hammer that floods the board with Khorne summoned units and mounted elites rather than the Berzerker-core you'd expect from World Eaters.

The engine is Skarbrand's aura stripping Rage tokens to spike nearby Bloodletters and Bloodcrushers into extra attacks, with the Lord on Juggernaut delivering charge-reroll threats that force the opponent to choose between contesting mid-board objectives or absorbing a T6 cavalry crash turn 2.

The 4+ invuln on Bloodcrushers combined with Flesh Hound screens punishes Heavy Gunline Toolbox lists that can't clear the screen fast enough — Russ Demolishers eat the Hound chaff while the Crusher brick and Skarbrand close the distance unmolested.

The list's near-coin-flip win rate signals the core weakness: it has no answer to AP-3+ melta concentration from Mobile Anti-Armour lists, and without Disgustingly Resilient or reanimation the daemon units evaporate under focused Knight Despoiler or Mont'ka Riptide fire before the charge resolves.
